title: Offer & Negotiation
description: Salary, start date, benefits, and polite counter-offers.

items.scenario: You received a written offer. Base salary is 10% below your target. You still want the role.

choices.text: This offer is insulting. Fix it.
Thank you for the offer. I am excited about the role. Based on market data and my scope in reliability ownership, I am targeting X base. Is there flexibility to move closer to that number?
I will only accept if you match my dream number today.
Ignore the offer email for a week to create pressure.

items.explanation: Gratitude + enthusiasm + data-backed ask + collaborative question.

items.scenario: Recruiter asks for your current salary before sharing a range.

choices.text: I make very little, so anything is fine.
I prefer to focus on the range for this role and the market. What budget range has been approved for this position?
I refuse to talk numbers ever.
Tell me the max and I will take it.

items.explanation: Redirect to role budget without oversharing or sounding hostile.

items.scenario: The company cannot raise base much but offers a signing bonus and earlier equity refresh.

choices.text: Base is all that matters; reject everything else.
I appreciate the creative package. Could we confirm the signing bonus amount, vesting timing, and whether a six-month salary review is possible? I want the total package to reflect the scope.
Fine, whatever.
I need unlimited equity forever.

items.explanation: Evaluate total comp components and ask clarifying structure questions.

items.scenario: You are negotiating an IT Manager offer and want clarity on team size and budget authority.

choices.text: Can I fire anyone in week one?
Before I accept, I would like written clarity on team size, hiring plan for the next two quarters, and decision rights for tooling budget. That helps me commit to the outcomes we discussed.
Titles do not matter; skip the details.
I will figure out authority after I join.

items.explanation: Senior negotiation includes scope and authority, not only money.

items.scenario: They ask if you can start in one week. You need three weeks to hand over your current job.

choices.text: Sure, I will ghost my current employer.
I can start on [date in three weeks]. I want to complete a clean handover at my current company. If helpful, I can do limited onboarding reading before day one.
I might start someday.
Take it or leave it: two months from now only.

items.explanation: Protect professionalism with a firm date and optional light prep.

items.scenario: Two offers are open. Company A is your preference but slower on paperwork.
items.prompt: How do you buy time politely with Company B?

choices.text: Lie and say you are sick.
I am very interested and want to give this decision proper attention. Could I confirm by Friday? I will keep you updated if anything changes sooner.
Tell them you already signed elsewhere.
Stop answering emails.

items.explanation: Ask for a concrete extension without burning goodwill.

items.scenario: Remote policy is unclear in the offer letter.
items.prompt: What should you clarify in writing?

choices.text: I assume remote forever with no questions.
Could we add the remote/hybrid expectation to the offer: work location, core collaboration hours, and travel frequency for onsite planning? I want alignment before signing.
Policies always change, so skip it.
Only ask after your first performance review.

items.explanation: Put location and travel expectations in writing before you accept.

items.scenario: HR says benefits are standard and not negotiable. You care about learning budget.

choices.text: Standard is unacceptable.
Understood on core benefits. Is there flexibility for an annual learning budget or conference stipend? Professional development is important for the SRE craft I will bring to the team.
Forget benefits; only cash.
Demand a company car.

items.explanation: Accept constraints, then ask for adjacent levers tied to role value.

items.scenario: You want to accept verbally but wait for the written offer.

choices.text: I accept; no need for paperwork.
I am prepared to accept contingent on receiving the written offer that reflects what we discussed on base, start date, and title. Please send it over and I will sign promptly.
Maybe I accept.
Send me something eventually.

items.explanation: Show intent while anchoring on written terms.

items.scenario: The offer includes a non-compete that seems broad for your region.

choices.text: Sign quietly and ignore it.
I am excited to move forward. Before signing, I would like to review the non-compete scope and duration with counsel and discuss a narrower version that still protects the company’s interests.
Refuse all legal documents.
Post the contract on social media for advice.

items.explanation: Stay collaborative while protecting yourself through review and scoped edits.

items.scenario: Recruiter asks why you are countering.

choices.text: Because I can.
Because the scope includes on-call leadership and cross-team delivery ownership. The counter aligns compensation with that responsibility and current market ranges for similar roles.
Your first number was a test.
My friend got more at another company, end of story.

items.explanation: Tie the counter to scope and market, not ego.

items.scenario: You decide to decline an offer after negotiating.

choices.text: Your offer was a joke.
Thank you for the offer and the thoughtful process. After careful consideration I will not be moving forward. I have a lot of respect for the team and hope our paths cross again.
No reply needed.
Accept then resign in week one.

items.explanation: Decline with gratitude and leave the door open.
